question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The project fell besides due to lack of funding and support.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. fell through due to lack.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "fall through" means to fail; to not happen or not be completed (of a plan/deal). The project failed for lack of funding, so "fell through". (विफल हो जाना / पूरा न हो पाना)

◦ Correct: The project fell through due to lack of funding and support.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "fell besides / along / about / until" are not valid phrasal verbs conveying failure.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "fall": fall through (fail to happen), fall out (quarrel), fall back on (rely on), fall behind (lag), fall apart (break down).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Panacea
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Remedy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Panacea" means a solution or remedy for all difficulties or diseases; a cure-all. Its closest synonym is "remedy". (रामबाण / सर्वरोग निवारक)

◦ Example: Education is not a panacea for all social problems, but it helps.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Survey" (examination), Option 3 "Pressure" (force) and Option 4 "Miracle" (a wonderful event) are not exact synonyms.

NOTE

• Synonyms of panacea: cure-all, remedy, universal cure, elixir. The word comes from Greek "Panakeia", the goddess of universal remedy.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

My sister-in-law is the most succeeded for all the industrialists in this country today.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. succeeded for all.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Succeeded" is a verb (past tense of "succeed"), but here an adjective is needed with the superlative "the most", and the correct preposition is "among". So it should be "the most successful among all the industrialists".

◦ Correct: My sister-in-law is the most successful among all the industrialists in this country today.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "in this country today", "My sister-in-law is the most" and "the industrialists" are acceptable.

NOTE

• Word forms: succeed (verb), success (noun), successful (adjective), successfully (adverb). Use "among" (not "for") when singling out one from a group; "the most successful among the group".

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I hope that / yesterday's lunch / at Rahul's place / was at your liking.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. was at your liking.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct idiom/expression is "to one's liking" (meaning "as one likes it / satisfactory"), which uses the preposition "to", not "at". So it should be "to your liking".

◦ Correct: I hope that yesterday's lunch at Rahul's place was to your liking.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "I hope that", "yesterday's lunch" and "at Rahul's place" are all correct.

NOTE

• "To one's liking" = pleasing/satisfactory to someone. Similar expressions: "to one's taste", "to one's satisfaction". Note the fixed preposition "to".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The lenient ways of the manager prompted substandard work from his subordinates.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. easygoing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lenient" means not strict; merciful, tolerant or permissive. Its closest synonym is "easygoing" (relaxed and tolerant). (उदार / नरम)

◦ Example: The lenient/easygoing teacher rarely punished the students.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "ignorant" (lacking knowledge), Option 3 "irritating" (annoying) and Option 4 "insane" (mad) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of lenient: easygoing, tolerant, merciful, indulgent, permissive.

• Antonyms: strict, severe, harsh, rigid, stern.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Medicin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Medicin" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Medicine", meaning a substance used to treat or prevent disease. (दवा / औषधि)

◦ Example: The doctor prescribed some medicine for the fever.

• Spelling key: MED + I + CINE — it ends in "-cine" (the final "e" is essential).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Addict", "Crazy" and "Eighty" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related words: medical, medication, medicinal, medicine. Remember the final "e" in medicine (unlike some words, it is not dropped).

question:
Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

Everyone says that waking up early in the morning is beneficial for our health and overall well-being. But it is easier said than done.
option_3: to start performing better than before
option_4: not as easy as it seems to be
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. not as easy as it seems to be.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "easier said than done" means something is much more difficult to do in practice than it is to talk about; not as easy as it seems. (कहना आसान, करना मुश्किल)

◦ Example: Losing weight is easier said than done.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 3 do not convey the sense that the task is harder to do than to say.

NOTE

• Similar idioms about difficulty: "a tall order" (a difficult task), "no walk in the park", "no bed of roses".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The management gave kudos to Jithin for his performance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. praise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kudos" means praise, credit or admiration for an achievement. Its closest synonym is "praise". (प्रशंसा / सराहना)

◦ Example: She received kudos/praise for her excellent presentation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "criticism", Option 3 "punishment" and Option 4 "admonishment" (a scolding) are all opposite in sense.

NOTE

• "Kudos" comes from Greek, meaning "glory/renown". Synonyms: praise, acclaim, credit, applause, recognition. Antonyms: criticism, blame, censure.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

The White man had to swallow his bombast and have completed the journey in mortified.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. complete the journey in mortification.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After "had to", we use the base form of the verb — "had to swallow ... and (had to) complete the journey". Also, "mortified" (an adjective/participle) is wrong here; the noun "mortification" (shame/humiliation) is needed after "in".

◦ Correct: The White man had to swallow his bombast and complete the journey in mortification.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 keeps the wrong "have completed ... in mortified".

• Options 3 and 4 use wrong verb forms/word order.

NOTE

• "Had to + base verb" (had to complete). "Mortification" (noun) = a feeling of humiliation/shame; "mortified" (adjective) = feeling humiliated; "mortifying" (adjective) = causing humiliation.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Hamper
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Hinder.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hamper" (as a verb) means to hinder, obstruct or prevent the progress of something. Its closest synonym is "hinder". (बाधा डालना / रोकना)

◦ Example: Heavy rain hampered/hindered the rescue operations.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Urge" (to encourage strongly), Option 3 "Accuse" (to charge with wrongdoing) and Option 4 "Absorb" (to soak up) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of hamper: hinder, obstruct, impede, hamstring, block.

• Antonyms: help, aid, assist, facilitate. ("Hamper" as a noun also means a basket for food.)

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

During the meeting, the employer's __________ was clear as he calmly addressed each team member's concerns and provided insightful solutions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. composure.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A noun is needed as the subject after "the employer's". "Composure" (a noun) means calmness and self-control, which fits "he calmly addressed ... concerns". (शांति / धैर्य)

◦ Correct: During the meeting, the employer's composure was clear ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "composes" and 2 "compose" are verbs; Option 4 "composed" is a past tense/adjective — none can be the noun subject required here.

NOTE

• Word forms: compose (verb), composure (noun — calmness), composed (adjective — calm), composition (noun — a piece of writing/music).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The new intern was eager to learn the __________ of the corporate world.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. ropes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to learn the ropes" means to learn how to do a particular job or task; to become familiar with the way something works. (कामकाज सीखना)

◦ Example: It took the trainee a month to learn the ropes of the new job.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "learn the rides/tides/flies" are not valid idioms.

NOTE

• The idiom comes from sailing, where new sailors had to learn how to handle the many ropes on a ship. Related: "show someone the ropes" (to teach someone how to do a job).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

While she / was watched / the movie, / her phone rang.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. was watched.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The context requires the past continuous active — "was watching" (an ongoing action interrupted by another). "Was watched" is passive and wrong here.

◦ Correct: While she was watching the movie, her phone rang.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "While she", "the movie," and "her phone rang" are all correct.

NOTE

• Structure: "While + past continuous (was/were + V-ing) ... simple past" — a longer action (watching) interrupted by a shorter one (the phone rang).

question:
Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The flight was about to take off when suddenly the authorities came to ensure the record of the maintanance department.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. maintenance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "maintenance", meaning the process of keeping something in good condition/working order. (रख-रखाव / अनुरक्षण)

◦ Example: The machines need regular maintenance.

• Spelling key: MAIN + TEN + ANCE — note "ten" in the middle (though the verb is "maintain", the noun drops the "i" → maintenance).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 4 ("maintnance", "maintainance", "maintainence") are all misspellings.

NOTE

• Note the spelling change: verb "maintain" → noun "maintenance" (the "ai" becomes "e"). Similarly: pronounce → pronunciation, explain → explanation.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Sarah / will singing / at the concert / on Saturday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. will singing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Will" is a modal and must be followed by the base form of the verb (will sing) or by "be + V-ing" for the future continuous (will be singing). "Will singing" is grammatically wrong.

◦ Correct: Sarah will sing (or will be singing) at the concert on Saturday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Sarah", "at the concert" and "on Saturday" are all correct.

NOTE

• After the modal "will": will + base verb (will sing) = simple future; will + be + V-ing (will be singing) = future continuous. Never "will + V-ing" alone.

question:
Select the most appropriate verb / verb phrase to fill in the blank.

In 2030, advancements in technology __________ the way we live, work and interact with each other.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. will be reshaping.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The time reference "In 2030" points to a future ongoing action, so the future continuous tense (will be + V-ing) is most appropriate — "advancements in technology will be reshaping the way we live". (भविष्य में निरंतर क्रिया)

◦ Correct: In 2030, advancements in technology will be reshaping the way we live, work and interact.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "could be reshaped" is passive/uncertain; Option 2 "shall have been reshaped" is future perfect passive (wrong sense); Option 4 "have reshaped" is present perfect (wrong tense for the future 2030).

NOTE

• Future continuous (will be + V-ing) describes an action that will be in progress at a specific future time — here, the ongoing transformation by 2030.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

They were / interested / on / learning new languages.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. on.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adjective "interested" is followed by the preposition "in", not "on". So it should be "interested in learning new languages".

◦ Correct: They were interested in learning new languages.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "They were", "interested" and "learning new languages" are all correct.

NOTE

• Adjective + preposition collocations: interested in, good at, afraid of, fond of, proud of, keen on, capable of. Note that after "interested in", we use a gerund (interested in learning).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Colloquiel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Colloquiel" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Colloquial", meaning relating to ordinary or informal conversation (not formal or literary language). (बोलचाल का / अनौपचारिक)

◦ Example: "Gonna" is a colloquial form of "going to".

• Spelling key: COL + LO + QUI + AL — ends in "-quial" (not "-quiel").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Posthumous" (occurring after death), "Extraneous" (irrelevant/external) and "Quiescent" (inactive/dormant) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related words: colloquial, colloquialism, colloquially. Words with "-quial/-quy": colloquial, soliloquy, ventriloquist.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The way she elaborated on every detail with precision impressed everyone _____ the meeting.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. at.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "at" is used with events/gatherings such as a meeting, a party or a conference — "everyone at the meeting". (बैठक में)

◦ Correct: ... impressed everyone at the meeting.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "off", Option 2 "above" and Option 4 "into" do not fit the sense of people present at an event.

NOTE

• Use "at" for events and specific points: at the meeting, at the party, at the concert, at the bus stop, at 5 o'clock.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the following word.

Reluctant
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Unwilling.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Reluctant" means unwilling and hesitant; disinclined to do something. Its closest synonym is "unwilling". (अनिच्छुक)

◦ Example: He was reluctant/unwilling to leave his hometown.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Unrelenting" (not yielding / relentless), Option 3 "Curious" (eager to know) and Option 4 "Pleasant" (agreeable) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of reluctant: unwilling, hesitant, disinclined, averse, loath.

• Antonyms: willing, eager, keen, enthusiastic.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

A phobia is an irrational fear of an object, situation or living thing. While fear is (1)_______ natural response to danger, phobias often occur (2)_______ response to something unlikely to cause real harm. In some cases, a person with a (3)_______ will meet the diagnostic criteria for a specific phobia, which is a type of anxiety disorder. Someone with a specific phobia will (4)_______ intense fear and anxiety when confronted with the source of the phobia, which could include blood, heights or specific animals like dogs. Phobias are (5)_______ by significant distress and often cause a person to avoid the source of their fear or suffer from extreme anxiety when faced with it. Someone experiencing a phobia that is interfering with everyday life should consider undergoing treatment for their phobia, as outcomes for professional care are typically favourable.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. a.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The indefinite article "a" is needed before the singular countable noun phrase "natural response" — "fear is a natural response to danger". (एकवचन गणनीय संज्ञा के लिए 'a')

◦ Correct: While fear is a natural response to danger ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "one" is possible but "a" is the natural choice for a general singular noun.

• Options 3 "those" and 4 "these" are plural demonstratives and do not fit "response" (singular).

NOTE

• Use "a/an" before singular countable nouns mentioned generally: "a natural response", "an idea", "a solution".

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

A phobia is an irrational fear of an object, situation or living thing. While fear is (1)_______ natural response to danger, phobias often occur (2)_______ response to something unlikely to cause real harm. In some cases, a person with a (3)_______ will meet the diagnostic criteria for a specific phobia, which is a type of anxiety disorder. Someone with a specific phobia will (4)_______ intense fear and anxiety when confronted with the source of the phobia, which could include blood, heights or specific animals like dogs. Phobias are (5)_______ by significant distress and often cause a person to avoid the source of their fear or suffer from extreme anxiety when faced with it. Someone experiencing a phobia that is interfering with everyday life should consider undergoing treatment for their phobia, as outcomes for professional care are typically favourable.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. in.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed phrase is "in response to", meaning "as a reaction to". So "phobias often occur in response to something ...". (के जवाब में / प्रतिक्रिया में)

◦ Correct: ... phobias often occur in response to something unlikely to cause real harm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "on/of/at response to" are not correct collocations.

NOTE

• Fixed prepositional phrase: "in response to" (something). Similar: in reaction to, in reply to, in answer to.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

A phobia is an irrational fear of an object, situation or living thing. While fear is (1)_______ natural response to danger, phobias often occur (2)_______ response to something unlikely to cause real harm. In some cases, a person with a (3)_______ will meet the diagnostic criteria for a specific phobia, which is a type of anxiety disorder. Someone with a specific phobia will (4)_______ intense fear and anxiety when confronted with the source of the phobia, which could include blood, heights or specific animals like dogs. Phobias are (5)_______ by significant distress and often cause a person to avoid the source of their fear or suffer from extreme anxiety when faced with it. Someone experiencing a phobia that is interfering with everyday life should consider undergoing treatment for their phobia, as outcomes for professional care are typically favourable.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. phobia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage is about phobias, and the sentence says a person "with a ___ will meet the diagnostic criteria for a specific phobia". The logical word is "phobia" — a person with a phobia will meet the criteria for a specific phobia. (भय / फोबिया)

◦ Correct: ... a person with a phobia will meet the diagnostic criteria for a specific phobia ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "violence", 2 "danger" and 4 "trouble" do not fit the medical/diagnostic context of the sentence.

NOTE

• Read the whole sentence for context. The repetition/link with "a specific phobia" makes "phobia" the natural fit for the blank.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

A phobia is an irrational fear of an object, situation or living thing. While fear is (1)_______ natural response to danger, phobias often occur (2)_______ response to something unlikely to cause real harm. In some cases, a person with a (3)_______ will meet the diagnostic criteria for a specific phobia, which is a type of anxiety disorder. Someone with a specific phobia will (4)_______ intense fear and anxiety when confronted with the source of the phobia, which could include blood, heights or specific animals like dogs. Phobias are (5)_______ by significant distress and often cause a person to avoid the source of their fear or suffer from extreme anxiety when faced with it. Someone experiencing a phobia that is interfering with everyday life should consider undergoing treatment for their phobia, as outcomes for professional care are typically favourable.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. experience.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Experience" (as a verb) means to feel or undergo (something). Someone with a specific phobia will "experience intense fear and anxiety" when facing the source of the phobia. (अनुभव करना)

◦ Correct: Someone with a specific phobia will experience intense fear and anxiety ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "horizon" is a noun; Option 2 "aspire" (to hope/aim) and Option 3 "dream" do not fit "intense fear and anxiety".

NOTE

• "Experience" as a verb collocates with feelings/events: experience fear, pain, joy, difficulty. It is the natural verb after "will" here.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

A phobia is an irrational fear of an object, situation or living thing. While fear is (1)_______ natural response to danger, phobias often occur (2)_______ response to something unlikely to cause real harm. In some cases, a person with a (3)_______ will meet the diagnostic criteria for a specific phobia, which is a type of anxiety disorder. Someone with a specific phobia will (4)_______ intense fear and anxiety when confronted with the source of the phobia, which could include blood, heights or specific animals like dogs. Phobias are (5)_______ by significant distress and often cause a person to avoid the source of their fear or suffer from extreme anxiety when faced with it. Someone experiencing a phobia that is interfering with everyday life should consider undergoing treatment for their phobia, as outcomes for professional care are typically favourable.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. characterised.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "To be characterised by" means to have as a typical or distinguishing feature. Phobias are typically marked by significant distress, so "Phobias are characterised by significant distress". (की विशेषता होना)

◦ Correct: Phobias are characterised by significant distress ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "classified" and Option 4 "categorised" take "as/into", not "by".

• Option 2 "qualified" does not fit the sense of a distinguishing feature.

NOTE

• Fixed collocation: "characterised by (a feature)". Compare: "classified as/into groups", "categorised into types". Here "by" signals "characterised".

question: How much money was allotted by the Gujarat government in August 2023 for the One District, One Product (ODOP) Programme to promote its indigenous products at the international level?
solution_text:
The correct answer is ₹58 crore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In August 2023, the Gujarat government allotted about ₹58 crore for the "One District, One Product (ODOP)" programme to promote its indigenous/local products at the international level. (ओडीओपी — गुजरात, ₹58 करोड़)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The ODOP initiative aims to identify and promote one distinctive product from each district, boosting local manufacturing, employment and exports.

• It aligns with the "Vocal for Local" and "Atmanirbhar Bharat" vision.

NOTE

• ODOP is often linked with GI (Geographical Indication) tags. Examples: Bhagalpur silk (Bihar), Firozabad glassware (UP), Kanchipuram silk (Tamil Nadu).

question: In the context of microfinance in India, the concept of SHG-BLP is used. What does L stand for in SHG-BLP?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Linkage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In microfinance, "SHG-BLP" stands for the "Self Help Group – Bank Linkage Programme". Here, "L" stands for "Linkage". (एसएचजी-बैंक लिंकेज कार्यक्रम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme was launched by NABARD in 1992 to connect Self Help Groups (SHGs) with the formal banking system for savings and credit.

• It is one of the largest microfinance programmes in the world and a major tool for financial inclusion and women's empowerment.

NOTE

• A Self Help Group (SHG) is a small voluntary group (usually 10–20 members, often women) who pool savings and provide small loans to members.

question: In which among the following years was Hindu widow remarriage declared legal in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1856.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Hindu widow remarriage was legalised in 1856 through the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856. The Act was passed largely due to the efforts of the social reformer Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar. (हिंदू विधवा पुनर्विवाह अधिनियम — 1856)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Act was passed during the governor-generalship of Lord Canning (Lord Dalhousie initiated it).

• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a great educationist and reformer of Bengal who also worked for women's education.

NOTE

• Other reform legislation: Abolition of Sati (1829, Lord Bentinck), Age of Consent Act (1891), Child Marriage Restraint (Sarda) Act (1929).

question: Annapurna Devi is associated with which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Surbahar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Annapurna Devi was a renowned Hindustani classical musician associated with the Surbahar (a bass sitar). She belonged to the Maihar gharana and was a disciple/daughter of Ustad Allauddin Khan. (सुरबहार — अन्नपूर्णा देवी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Surbahar is a plucked string instrument similar to the sitar but larger, producing a deeper, bass sound.

• Annapurna Devi was awarded the Padma Bhushan; she was known for her reclusive life and dedication to teaching.

NOTE

• Instrument–artist pairs: Sitar (Ravi Shankar), Sarod (Amjad Ali Khan), Flute (Hariprasad Chaurasia), Sarangi (Ram Narayan), Santoor (Shivkumar Sharma).

question: Who regarded Vedas as the source of all knowledge and known for the slogan 'Go back to the Vedas'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swami Dayanada Saraswati.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Swami Dayananda Saraswati, the founder of the Arya Samaj (1875), regarded the Vedas as the source of all true knowledge and gave the famous slogan "Go Back to the Vedas". (वेदों की ओर लौटो — स्वामी दयानंद सरस्वती)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• He wrote "Satyarth Prakash" (The Light of Truth) and opposed idol worship, casteism, child marriage and superstitions.

• The Arya Samaj promoted women's education, widow remarriage and the Shuddhi movement; it founded DAV (Dayanand Anglo-Vedic) institutions.

NOTE

• Other reformers: Raja Ram Mohan Roy (Brahmo Samaj, 1828), Swami Vivekananda (Ramakrishna Mission, 1897), Keshab Chandra Sen (Brahmo Samaj leader).

question: Rigveda is the earliest specimen of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indo European language.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rigveda is the earliest specimen (oldest surviving text) of the Indo-European language family. It is composed in Vedic Sanskrit, which belongs to the Indo-Aryan branch of the Indo-European languages. (ऋग्वेद — इंडो-यूरोपीय भाषा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas (Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, Atharvaveda) and is a collection of hymns (suktas) dedicated to various deities.

• The Indo-European language family includes Sanskrit, Latin, Greek, Persian, and most European languages.

NOTE

• The Gayatri Mantra is from the Rigveda. The Rigveda's 10th Mandala contains the Purushasukta, which mentions the four varnas.

question: What is the length of the men's kabaddi court?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 13 m.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The standard men's kabaddi court measures 13 metres in length and 10 metres in width. (पुरुष कबड्डी कोर्ट — 13 मीटर लंबाई)

• For women (and juniors), the court is slightly smaller — 12 m × 8 m.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kabaddi is a traditional Indian contact team sport; a "raider" enters the opponents' half chanting "kabaddi" and tries to tag defenders and return.

• India has dominated the Kabaddi World Cup and the sport is popular through the Pro Kabaddi League (PKL).

NOTE

• Court dimensions for SSC: Kabaddi (men) 13 m × 10 m, Hockey 91.4 m × 55 m, Cricket pitch 22 yards (20.12 m).

question: Which of the given options is rod-shaped, carries genetic information, is visible only at cell division and is present in the nucleus?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chromosomes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Chromosomes" are rod-shaped (thread-like) structures present in the nucleus that carry the genetic information (DNA/genes) and become clearly visible only during cell division. (गुणसूत्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Humans have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs) in each body cell, including one pair of sex chromosomes (XX in females, XY in males).

• A chromosome is made of DNA and proteins (histones); a segment of DNA that codes for a trait is called a gene.

NOTE

• Lysosomes are "suicidal bags"; ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis; cytoplasm is the jelly-like fluid of the cell. Only chromosomes carry hereditary information.

question: Prerana Shrimali received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in which of the following years for her contribution to the Kathak dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2009.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Prerana Shrimali, a distinguished Kathak dancer, received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2009 for her contribution to the dance form. (प्रेरणा श्रीमाली — कथक — 2009)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Prerana Shrimali is associated with the Jaipur gharana of Kathak and was a disciple of Kundan Lal Gangani.

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, established in 1952, is India's national academy for music, dance and drama.

NOTE

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dances, mainly of North India, known for fast footwork (tatkar), spins (chakkars) and abhinaya. Its main gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

question: Which gas is released when you combine vinegar and baking soda in a balloon, causing it to inflate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carbon dioxide.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When vinegar (acetic acid) reacts with baking soda (sodium bicarbonate), it releases carbon dioxide (CO₂) gas, which inflates the balloon. (कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड)

◦ Reaction: NaHCO₃ + CH₃COOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂↑

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• This is a classic acid–base (neutralisation) reaction that produces a salt, water and carbon dioxide gas.

• The same principle (release of CO₂) is used by baking soda/baking powder to make cakes and bread rise.

NOTE

• CO₂ turns lime water milky and does not support combustion (it is used in fire extinguishers). It is also released during respiration and fermentation.

question: From 13 September 2023, DMK MP Tiruchi Siva has been appointed the chairperson of the Committee on __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Industry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• From 13 September 2023, DMK MP Tiruchi Siva was appointed the Chairperson of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry. (उद्योग संबंधी समिति — तिरुचि शिवा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Parliamentary Standing Committees examine bills, budgets and policies in detail and assist Parliament in its oversight function.

• They are broadly of two types: Standing Committees (permanent) and Ad hoc Committees (temporary).

NOTE

• The Department-Related Standing Committees (DRSCs) were introduced in 1993; they help in the detailed scrutiny of the demands for grants and bills of various ministries.

question:
Which of the following Rights is mentioned in Article 21 of the Indian Constitution?

A) Right to Freedom: Protection of life and personal liberty  B) Right against Exploitation: Prohibition of trafficking in human beings and forced labour  C) Right to Equality: Equality before law  D) Right to Freedom of Religion: Freedom to manage religious affairs
option_1: Right to Freedom: Protection of life and personal liberty
option_2: Right against Exploitation: Prohibition of trafficking in human beings and forced labour
option_3: Right to Equality: Equality before law
option_4: Right to Freedom of Religion: Freedom to manage religious affairs
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right to Freedom: Protection of life and personal liberty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 21 of the Constitution guarantees the "Protection of Life and Personal Liberty" — no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. It is part of the Right to Freedom (Articles 19–22). (अनुच्छेद 21 — प्राण एवं दैहिक स्वतंत्रता का संरक्षण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Over time, Article 21 has been widely interpreted by the Supreme Court to include the right to a dignified life, livelihood, privacy, clean environment, education (Article 21A) and more.

• Along with Article 20, Article 21 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency (44th Amendment).

NOTE

• The other options wrongly match the articles: Article 14 (Equality before law), Article 23 (against trafficking/forced labour), Article 26 (manage religious affairs).

question: The Sahitya Akademi award winning novel 'Zindaginama' was written by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Krishna Sobti.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Hindi novel "Zindaginama" was written by Krishna Sobti, for which she received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1980. (ज़िंदगीनामा — कृष्णा सोबती)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Krishna Sobti is a celebrated Hindi writer; she was also awarded the Jnanpith Award (2017), India's highest literary honour.

• Her other notable works include "Mitro Marjani", "Dil-o-Danish" and "Ai Ladki".

NOTE

• Amrita Pritam (Punjabi writer — "Pinjar"), Mahadevi Verma (a poet of the Chhayavaad movement) and Mannu Bhandari ("Aapka Bunty") are other major Hindi/Punjabi literary figures.

question: Who among the following is worshipped as Nataraja before many classical dance performances in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shiva.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lord Shiva, in his form as "Nataraja" (the "King/Lord of Dance"), is worshipped before many classical dance performances in India. Nataraja represents Shiva performing the cosmic dance (Tandava). (नटराज — भगवान शिव)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Nataraja form shows Shiva dancing within a ring of flames, symbolising the cosmic cycle of creation and destruction.

• The famous Nataraja temple is at Chidambaram (Tamil Nadu).

NOTE

• The Tandava is the vigorous, masculine dance of Shiva; the Lasya is the gentle, graceful dance associated with Parvati. Nataraja bronzes are masterpieces of Chola art.

question: The famous 'Tripartite struggle' for supremacy occurred between which of the following powers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gurjar-Pratihara, Rashtrakuta and Palas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous "Tripartite Struggle" (8th–9th centuries CE) was fought among three powerful dynasties — the Gurjara-Pratiharas, the Rashtrakutas and the Palas — for control over the city of Kannauj (Kanyakubja), which was a symbol of sovereignty over North India. (त्रिपक्षीय संघर्ष — कन्नौज हेतु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kannauj was strategically important and prestigious; whoever controlled it was seen as the paramount power of North India.

• The Gurjara-Pratiharas ultimately gained control of Kannauj for a long period.

NOTE

• Key rulers: Gurjara-Pratihara (Nagabhata I, Mihira Bhoja), Rashtrakuta (Dhruva, Govinda III), Pala (Dharmapala, Devapala). The struggle weakened all three, aiding later invasions.

question: Four resistors of equal resistance R each are connected in various possible ways both in series and/or parallel to get different combined resistances. Which of the following values of resistance cannot be achieved by using all the four resistors?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2 R.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Using all four equal resistors (R each), the value "2 R" cannot be obtained in any valid series/parallel combination, whereas the others can:

◦ 0.25 R = all four in parallel (R/4 = 0.25 R).

◦ 1.33 R = one resistor in series with three resistors in parallel (R + R/3 = 4R/3 ≈ 1.33 R).

◦ 2.5 R = two in series (2R) + two in parallel (R/2) → 2R + 0.5R = 2.5 R.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Series: R_total = R₁ + R₂ + ... (resistances add up).

• Parallel: 1/R_total = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + ... (for equal resistors in parallel, R_total = R/n).

NOTE

• In series, the total resistance is more than the largest; in parallel, it is less than the smallest. Combining series and parallel gives intermediate values.

question: The remains of Great Bath have been found from the excavation at which of the following Harappan sites?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mohenjodaro.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous "Great Bath" — a large, watertight tank used possibly for ritual bathing — was found at the Harappan site of Mohenjo-daro (in present-day Sindh, Pakistan). (महान स्नानागार — मोहनजोदड़ो)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Great Bath is one of the earliest public water tanks; it was made watertight using bitumen (natural tar) and finely fitted bricks.

• Mohenjo-daro ("Mound of the Dead") was excavated by R. D. Banerji (1922) and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

NOTE

• Site–feature pairs: Great Bath & Great Granary (Mohenjo-daro), Dockyard (Lothal), Ploughed field & fire altars (Kalibangan), Rows of granaries (Harappa).

question: As per HDI 2021, which of the following neighbouring countries of India had the highest female life expectancy at birth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maldives.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Human Development Index (HDI) 2021, among the given neighbouring countries of India, the Maldives had the highest female life expectancy at birth. (एचडीआई 2021 — मालदीव)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The HDI, published by the UNDP (United Nations Development Programme), measures development using three dimensions — health (life expectancy), education (years of schooling) and standard of living (GNI per capita).

• The HDI was developed by economists Mahbub ul Haq and Amartya Sen.

NOTE

• Life expectancy at birth is the average number of years a newborn is expected to live. It is a key indicator of the health and living conditions of a country.

question: What is the retirement age of Judges serving at the Supreme Court of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 65 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A Judge of the Supreme Court of India holds office until he/she attains the age of 65 years (retirement age). (उच्चतम न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश — 65 वर्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A High Court Judge retires at the age of 62 years.

• Supreme Court Judges are appointed by the President (Article 124); they can be removed only through impeachment for proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

NOTE

• The Supreme Court is the apex court of India (Article 124). The sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court is the Chief Justice + up to 33 other judges (34 in total).

question: According to the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare 2022-23, which state of India is the largest producer of sugarcane?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (2022-23), Uttar Pradesh is the largest producer of sugarcane in India. (उत्तर प्रदेश — गन्ना का सबसे बड़ा उत्पादक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Uttar Pradesh is followed by Maharashtra and Karnataka in sugarcane production.

• Sugarcane is a Kharif cash crop that needs a hot and humid climate; India is the second-largest producer of sugarcane in the world (after Brazil).

NOTE

• The sugar industry is the second-largest agro-based industry in India (after textiles). Sugarcane is the raw material for sugar, jaggery (gur), khandsari and ethanol.

question: Which of the following peaks is NOT located in the Himalayan mountains?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalsubai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kalsubai" is NOT a Himalayan peak — it is the highest peak in Maharashtra, located in the Western Ghats (Sahyadri range). (कलसुबाई — पश्चिमी घाट, हिमालय में नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Nanda Devi (Uttarakhand) and Kamet (Uttarakhand) are high peaks of the Himalayas.

• Annapurna is a Himalayan massif in Nepal.

NOTE

• Highest peaks by region: Kanchenjunga (highest in India, Himalayas), Anamudi (highest in South India, Western Ghats), Kalsubai (highest in Maharashtra), Doddabetta (Nilgiris).

question: Chithirai festival of Tamil Nadu is dedicated to which of the following Goddesses?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meenakshi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Chithirai festival" of Tamil Nadu, celebrated grandly at Madurai, is dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi. It marks the celestial wedding of Goddess Meenakshi with Lord Sundareswarar (Shiva). (चिथिराई महोत्सव — देवी मीनाक्षी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The festival is held at the famous Meenakshi Amman Temple in Madurai and is one of the largest festivals of Tamil Nadu.

• It usually takes place in the Tamil month of Chithirai (April–May).

NOTE

• The Meenakshi Temple at Madurai is a masterpiece of Dravidian architecture, known for its towering, colourful gopurams (gateway towers).

question: India won its first Olympic gold in hockey in which of the following years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1928.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India won its first Olympic gold medal in hockey at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics. This marked the beginning of India's golden era in hockey. (1928 एम्स्टर्डम ओलंपिक — भारत का पहला हॉकी स्वर्ण)

• The legendary Major Dhyan Chand was a star of that team.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• India won six consecutive Olympic hockey gold medals from 1928 to 1956 (1928, 1932, 1936, 1948, 1952, 1956).

• In all, India has won 8 Olympic gold medals in hockey.

NOTE

• Major Dhyan Chand is called the "Wizard/Magician of Hockey"; his birthday (29 August) is celebrated as National Sports Day.

question: The National Food Security Act (NFSA) was enacted in which year by the Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2013.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Food Security Act (NFSA) was enacted in 2013. It aims to provide subsidised foodgrains to about two-thirds of India's population (up to 75% of rural and 50% of urban population). (राष्ट्रीय खाद्य सुरक्षा अधिनियम — 2013)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Under the NFSA, eligible beneficiaries get foodgrains (rice, wheat, coarse grains) at highly subsidised prices through the Public Distribution System (PDS).

• It also has special provisions for pregnant women, lactating mothers and children (nutritional support), giving a legal "Right to Food".

NOTE

• The Act covers two categories: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) households (poorest) and Priority Households (PHH).

question: Gabbro is an example of which type of rocks?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Igneous rock.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gabbro" is an example of an igneous rock. It is a coarse-grained, intrusive (plutonic) igneous rock formed by the slow cooling and solidification of magma deep beneath the Earth's surface. (गैब्रो — आग्नेय चट्टान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Igneous rocks are formed by the cooling of magma/lava. They are of two types: intrusive/plutonic (cooled below the surface, e.g., granite, gabbro) and extrusive/volcanic (cooled on the surface, e.g., basalt).

• Igneous rocks are also called "primary rocks".

NOTE

• The three rock types: Igneous (from magma/lava), Sedimentary (from deposited sediments, e.g., sandstone, limestone) and Metamorphic (formed by heat/pressure, e.g., marble, slate).
